content.value_statement: Product teams often struggle to connect goals, epics, milestones, and sprint capacity. This skill guides collaborative planning with simple sizing, buffers, and roadmap files.
actual_capabilities: Structures quarterly roadmaps into epics, milestones, and sprint plans.
Applies a points-based capacity model for two-week sprints.
Guides collaborative planning by asking for goals, availability, and estimates.
Helps split milestones that are too large for one sprint.
Documents roadmap files under a .roadmap planning structure.
Describes ClickUp synchronization for epics, milestones, and status updates.
limitations: It provides planning guidance, not detailed product specifications or QA tracking.
It does not replace project management tools such as GitHub or ClickUp.
Capacity estimates depend on accurate team availability and honest sizing input.
ClickUp sync behavior depends on separate commands or integrations not included here.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Quarter
use_cases.description: Convert quarterly goals into epics, milestones, sprint allocations, and rough delivery expectations.

use_cases.title: Balance Engineering Capacity
use_cases.description: Estimate work with points, account for buffer time, and avoid overloading a two-week sprint.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Startup Roadmap
use_cases.description: Create a practical roadmap that connects major initiatives to delivery windows and team limits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Quarter
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a quarter for my team. Our goals are [goals], our team size is [team size], and our key constraints are [constraints].

prompt_templates.title: Break Down an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into milestones: [epic]. Estimate each milestone, identify risks, and suggest when to split oversized work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan our next two-week sprint. Available people are [people], current capacity is [capacity], and candidate milestones are [milestones].

prompt_templates.title: Review Roadmap Capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this roadmap against our capacity model. Find overloads, suggest tradeoffs, and propose a revised sequence for [quarter or release].

output_examples.input: Plan Q3 for three developers with two product goals and one support commitment.
output: The skill groups the goals into two epics and reserves buffer for support work.
It estimates each milestone with points and maps them across six two-week sprints.
It flags overloaded sprints and suggests moving lower-priority work later.

output_examples.input: Break a customer onboarding epic into milestones.
output: The output proposes discovery, workflow setup, invitation flows, analytics, and launch readiness milestones.
It identifies milestones above 25 points and recommends smaller checkpoints.
It notes dependencies that should be resolved before sprint allocation.

output_examples.input: Show whether Sprint 4 can fit the selected milestones.
output: The skill compares planned points against available capacity and a 15 percent buffer.
It explains which milestone should move if the sprint is over capacity.
It keeps the user involved before changing scope or dates.

best_practices: Provide team size, availability, known commitments, and target dates before planning.
Keep milestones coarse enough for roadmap tracking and small enough for sprint decisions.
Use the buffer consistently so urgent work does not break the plan.
anti_patterns: Using this skill to manage detailed tasks, pull requests, or QA checklists.
Treating point estimates as guarantees instead of planning signals.
Syncing roadmap data to ClickUp before confirming what should be shared.

faq.question: What planning level does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports quarterly roadmap planning, epic breakdown, milestone estimation, sprint allocation, and capacity review.

faq.question: Can it replace GitHub Issues or ClickUp?
faq.answer: No. It is a strategic planning layer and expects execution tracking to happen in dedicated tools.

faq.question: How does it estimate capacity?
faq.answer: It uses a two-week sprint model where one developer has about 20 points, with a recommended 15 percent buffer.

faq.question: Does it create detailed specifications?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on goals, rough size, timing, milestones, and sprint fit.

faq.question: Can it work with ClickUp?
faq.answer: The skill describes ClickUp push and pull commands for epics, milestones, and status updates. Confirm permissions before syncing data.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
